title: KV eviction race triggered streaming disconnects and partial tokens — action plan
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
During a regional capacity surge on 2026-01-25 we observed a pattern of customer streaming sessions disconnecting mid-response and a non-trivial percentage of sessions returning truncated/partial tokens. Total impacted requests peaked at ~5.1% of streaming traffic for 7 minutes. Root cause analysis indicates a race between the KV cache eviction path and the streaming sharding/hand-off logic when a worker is drained for autoscaling. A recent change to backpressure hysteresis (introduced in runtime-2.3-canary) unintentionally allowed the IO queue to accept new requests while the outbound streaming socket was in a transient half-closed state, causing token fragments to be ACKed but not forwarded to the original client connection.

What went wrong (summary):
- Autoscaler drained a worker during a burst; eviction of KV cache entries was synchronous and blocked the worker's streaming loop for up to ~120ms.
- The streaming hand-off code assumed in-flight KV state would be stable across a handoff boundary and did not consider the eviction path taking a lock that delayed the flush.
- Backpressure hysteresis change widened the window where new incoming requests were queued for a worker that had already half-closed its outbound socket, leading to token fragments being sent to the wrong connection context or dropped.
- Monitoring lacked an aggregate metric combining partial-token rates + per-socket half-close counts; paging thresholds were only set for full connection drops.

Detection and mitigation timeline (concise):
- 2026-01-25 09:14 UTC: Alert fired for elevated 5xx and streaming client disconnects (SRE pager).
- 09:16 UTC: Engineering on-call confirmed increase in partial-token telemetry and enabled additional tracing.
- 09:22 UTC: Emergency configuration rollback: backpressure hysteresis reverted in canary; immediate partial reduction in token truncations observed.
- 09:45 UTC: Temporary autoscaler drain threshold increased to delay worker drains during high QPS windows.
- 10:30 UTC: Post-incident triage and sampling of affected sessions; root cause work started.

Technical root causes (detailed):
- Blocking KV eviction: a synchronous eviction routine took an exclusive lock on the per-session KV shard during eviction, increasing tail latency and preventing timely flushes of the streaming output buffer.
- Handoff race: worker hand-off code did not atomically capture socket state + KV sequence numbers; a worker could publish that it was ready to hand off while its outbound socket was half-closed and its in-memory KV state mid-eviction.
- Hysteresis widening bug: a change intended to reduce oscillation allowed requests to queue to a draining worker for up to 200ms longer than intended without verifying socket liveness.

Immediate remediation already completed:
- Reverted hysteresis change in canary and rolled to the fleet (runtime-2.3-hotfix-1).
- Temporarily made KV eviction asynchronous with a bounded worker pool to avoid long blocking in the hot path. This is a stopgap; it reduces observed incidents but does not guarantee correct ordering across handoffs.
- Adjusted autoscaler drain policy to prefer draining empty workers and to add a cooldown during observed traffic spikes.
- Added an emergency alert combining partial-token-rate (>1%) AND per-socket half-close rate (>0.5%) to SRE pager.

Planned long-term fixes (action items below):
- Make KV eviction non-blocking for active sessions by implementing incremental eviction with safe snapshot semantics and sequence numbers. This prevents eviction from delaying streaming flushes. (Owner: Marco Li)
- Harden handoff protocol: atomically capture (socket-generation-id, KV-sequence) and reject handoff unless both are quiescent; introduce a short drain-window handshake to avoid in-flight fragments. (Owner: Priya Patel)
- Backpressure safety check: before accepting queued requests for a worker, confirm socket liveness and that outbound buffer has not been half-closed for >10ms. Reintroduce hysteresis with explicit socket checks. (Owner: Daniel Cho)
- Retroactive reconciliation job: scan recent session logs to detect mismatched token sequence IDs and attempt safe replays for eligible customers; create a customer outreach list for those with data loss. (Owner: SRE team lead: Elena Torres)
- E2E test harness: add a chaos test that simulates worker drains + KV eviction + backpressure to catch regressions in CI. (Owner: QA: Omar Rahman)

Acceptance criteria for fixes (required for Done):
- No partial-token incidents above 0.2% in production during synthetic 2x load tests for 24 hours.
- Handoff protocol unit tests and fuzz tests covering socket-generation mismatches added to runtime test suite.
- KV eviction completes without blocking the streaming loop for >15ms in 99.9% of traces.
- Pager thresholds tuned and verified in staging; SLOs updated and communicated to customer-facing teams.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Asynchronous eviction improves latency but risks eventual memory growth if eviction worker pool is saturated; we will add circuit-breakers and memory guards.
- Handoff atomicity adds a small latency cost (~2–5ms) to some handoffs; acceptable for correctness.

Customer impact and communication:
- Impact: multiple customers reported partial transcripts and a small number of reconnection loops. No data corruption of stored documents; primary impact was user-visible truncation and UX retries.
- Communication: PMs to prepare a short post-incident email for affected customers (template in attachments). SRE to include incident summary in weekly reliability digest.
postmortem_summary: This incident was caused by an interaction between a KV eviction lock path, a non-atomic streaming handoff, and a widened backpressure hysteresis window. Immediate rollbacks and temporary async eviction reduced impact. Long-term fixes focus on non-blocking eviction, atomic handoff semantics, and socket-aware backpressure checks. Action items assigned and E2E chaos tests planned.

ENG-91234-A3: Reintroduce hysteresis with socket liveness checks and small accept-window; add runtime feature-flag — Owner: Daniel Cho — due: 2026-02-28
ENG-91234-A4: Add chaos E2E test to CI (worker drain + eviction + backpressure) and run in canary pipeline — Owner: Omar Rahman — due: 2026-03-03
ENG-91234-A5: Retro-scanner job to detect affected sessions and prepare customer outreach — Owner: Elena Torres (SRE) — due: 2026-02-17
ENG-91234-A6: Update monitoring: partial-token-rate + half-close composite alert and dashboard tile — Owner: Monitoring Infra (owner TBD) — due: 2026-02-05
